routes.label: Find the common chord in coordinates

question: Semicircle \(\Gamma\) has diameter \(AB\) of length \(14.\) Circle \(\Omega\) lies tangent to \(AB\) at a point \(P\) and intersects \(\Gamma\) at points \(Q\) and \(R.\) If \(QR = 3\sqrt3\) and \(\angle QPR = 60^\circ,\) then the area of \(\triangle PQR\) is \(\dfrac{a\sqrt b}{c},\) where \(a\) and \(c\) are relatively prime positive integers and \(b\) is a positive integer not divisible by the square of any prime. What is \(a + b + c?\)
solution:
The useful construction is the midpoint of the common chord: both circle centers lie on its perpendicular bisector, creating right triangles with known lengths.

Let \(O_1\) be the center of the semicircle, \(O_2\) the center of \(\Omega\), and \(M\) the midpoint of \(QR\). The semicircle has radius \(7\), and
\[
QM=\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
Since \(\angle QPR=60^\circ\), the inscribed angle theorem gives the smaller central angle \(\angle QO_2R=120^\circ\). The perpendicular \(O_2M\) bisects this angle. Thus, if \(r\) is the radius of \(\Omega\),
\[
r=\frac{QM}{\sin60^\circ}=3,
\qquad O_2M=r\cos60^\circ=\frac32.
\]
For the larger circle, the Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
O_1M=\sqrt{7^2-\left(\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}\right)^2}
=\frac{13}{2}.
\]
The centers and \(M\) are collinear, so \(O_1O_2\) is either \(\tfrac{13}{2}-\tfrac32=5\) or \(\tfrac{13}{2}+\tfrac32=8\). Tangency gives \(O_2P\perp AB\) and \(O_2P=3\). If the center separation were \(8\), then
\[
O_1P=\sqrt{8^2-3^2}=\sqrt{55}>7,
\]
which is impossible because \(P\) lies on the diameter \(AB\). Consequently,
\[
O_1O_2=5,\qquad O_1P=\sqrt{5^2-3^2}=4.
\]
Also, \(M\) lies on ray \(O_1O_2\) beyond \(O_2\).

Let \(X\) be the intersection of lines \(QR\) and \(AB\). The right triangles \(XMO_1\) and \(O_2PO_1\) have the same acute angle at \(O_1\), so they are similar. Hence
\[
\frac{O_1X}{O_1O_2}=\frac{O_1M}{O_1P},
\qquad
O_1X=5\cdot\frac{13/2}{4}=\frac{65}{8}.
\]
Here \(X\) lies on ray \(O_1P\). Since \(O_1X>O_1P\), the point \(P\) lies between \(X\) and \(O_1\), giving
\[
XP=\frac{65}{8}-4=\frac{33}{8}.
\]
To find the height of \(\triangle PQR\), let \(H\) be the foot of the perpendicular from \(P\) to line \(QR\). The right triangles \(XHP\) and \(XMO_1\) share their angle at \(X\), so
\[
\frac{PH}{XP}=\frac{O_1M}{O_1X}
=\frac{13/2}{65/8}=\frac45.
\]
Therefore
\[
[\triangle PQR]
=\frac12\,QR\cdot PH
=\frac12\cdot3\sqrt3\cdot\frac{33}{8}\cdot\frac45
=\frac{99\sqrt3}{20}.
\]
Since \(99\) and \(20\) are relatively prime and \(3\) is squarefree, the requested sum is
\[
a+b+c=99+3+20=\boxed{122}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{D}\).
